# Research: How does routes() expose the payment service?

- Question: How does routes() expose the payment service?
- Slug: routes-shape
- Date: 2026-11-22
- Commit: d0b5ab6
- Requested by: kit-eval

## Findings

<!-- One bullet per claim. Every bullet ends with exactly one tag:
     [verified: path:START-END]   lines you read in this session; add a short quoted snippet in backticks
     [verified: cmd]              followed by a fenced block with the command and its output
     [docs: URL @ version]        official documentation at the pinned version from the lockfile
     [inferred: from F1,F2]       reasoning from tagged findings, listing their ids
     Hedge words (should, probably, likely, I think, assume) are not allowed here. -->

- F1. `routes()` takes the service as its parameter instead of importing an instance [verified: src/api/routes.ts:2-2] `export function routes(s: PaymentService)`
- F2. It returns a plain object with one operation, `charge`, which delegates to the service [verified: src/api/routes.ts:3-3] `return { charge: (u: string) => s.charge(u) };`
- F3. `PaymentService` has a `refund` method that no route exposes [verified: src/domain/payment.ts:6-8] `async refund(id: string)`
- F4. The service's database is a constructor parameter property, so a test passes a stub object [docs: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/classes.html#parameter-properties @ 5.5]
- F5. Exposing refunds means adding a `refund` key beside `charge` in the returned object [inferred: from F2,F3]

## What I could not verify

<!-- Each item is tagged [unknown] and names how to resolve it. Nothing here may be used as a basis for a decision. -->

- U1. Whether an HTTP layer mounts the object `routes()` returns [unknown] Resolve by: ask the owner; no server file exists in src/

## Notes

- An HTTP server probably mounts this object somewhere
- Adding refund should be safe since nothing else calls routes()

## Confidence

High — both files were read in full and the object has one key.

## Recommendation

Add a refund operation beside charge in the object (F2, F5); decide how it is mounted once U1 is answered.
